title: Dal Tadka
subtitle: Red lentil dal with a tempered spice finish
excerpt: A simple, satisfying Indian dal made from red lentils simmered with tomatoes, ginger, and garlic, then finished with a tadka of whole spices bloomed in hot oil. It takes about 35 minutes and keeps well for several days in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Based on the north Indian dal tadka, one of the most widely cooked everyday lentil dishes across India.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a larger saucepan.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. The tadka is best done fresh when reheating.

content.text: The tadka is the final step: whole spices are bloomed in hot oil for just a minute, then poured sizzling over the finished dal. Do not skip it; it makes a real difference to the depth of flavour.

items.prepNote: divided: 2 tbsp for dal, 1 tbsp for tadka

content.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of sunflower oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, coriander, and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, breaking them up with a spoon, until thickened.
Add the rinsed lentils and 700ml of water. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely soft and the dal is thick.
Season with salt and the lemon juice. Taste and adjust.

For the tadka, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a small pan over a high heat. Add the cumin seeds and mustard seeds. Cook for 30 to 45 seconds until they pop and smell fragrant, then immediately pour over the dal.
Top with fresh coriander and serve with rice or flatbreads.

items.cause: Lentils absorbed more water than expected
items.fix: Stir in a splash of water and heat through.

items.cause: Oil too hot or spices left in too long
items.fix: Keep the heat high but watch closely and pour after 45 seconds.
